section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Geometry of Oscillation
section_1.content: Establish the fundamental connection between uniform circular motion and sine/cosine waves. Use a visual 'shadow' projection where a point rotating on a circle creates a perfect sine wave on a time-axis graph.
section_1.example: A 'Robot Dog' walking in a circle; its shadow cast on a wall traces a perfect wave, representing the simplest harmonic oscillation.

section_2.title: Fourier's Core Concept: Building Complexity
section_2.content: Explain the Principle of Superposition: any periodic function can be reconstructed by summing simple sine and cosine waves of different frequencies. Introduce the 'Epicycle' visualization where rotating gears of varying sizes stack to trace a complex shape.
section_2.example: Stacking three gears of different speeds to transform a simple circular motion into the complex silhouette of a cat's profile.

section_3.title: Bridging to the Heat Equation
section_3.content: Introduce the Heat Equation: a Partial Differential Equation (PDE) describing how temperature diffuses over time. Explain that the Heat Equation has 'natural modes' of decay, which are sine/cosine functions. Thus, solving heat flow is equivalent to decomposing the initial temperature distribution into Fourier components.
section_3.example: A metal rod with a 'zig-zag' temperature distribution; as time passes, the Fourier components decay at different speeds, 'smoothing out' the rod's temperature.

section_4.title: Application: Thermal Diffusion in a Ring
section_4.content: Connect the linear heat equation to circular representations. By wrapping the rod into a ring (periodic boundary conditions), the Fourier series naturally emerges as the unique way to track heat flowing around the circle.
section_4.example: A circular 'Smart Heating Coil' inside an oven; the heat stabilizes into a smooth gradient, mathematically described by the sum of its Fourier modes.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap the logical chain: Circles produce Waves -> Waves combine into Series -> Series solve the Heat Equation -> Heat flow behaves like a symphony of decaying frequencies.
section_5.example: A visualization showing a complex thermal map on a circular sensor being 'unpacked' into its individual frequency components (the Fourier spectrum).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
